content.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `nth_largest` in `repo/ranking.py:6` — it used `n` directly as a list index, making it effectively 0-based. So "top 1" returned the 2nd largest, "top 2" the 3rd, and so on.

The fix was changing `return s[n]` to `return s[n - 1]`, so `n=1` now correctly returns the largest element. This also fixes the downstream callers for free:

- `rank_summary` in `repo/rows.py` — its `"top"` value was showing the 2nd largest instead of the max
- `old_nth_largest` in `repo/ranking.py` — the legacy wrapper delegates to `nth_largest`

Both tests in `tests/visible/test_rank.py` pass. I left the legacy wrapper itself alone since its TODO says it should only be removed after the v1 migration.
